questions.title: WITH Clause Purpose
questions.description: WITH dept AS (...) SELECT ... FROM dept — what does the WITH part do?
questions.Option2: Defines a named temporary result usable by the statement that follows

questions.title: CTE Lifetime
questions.description: A CTE exists:
questions.Option1: Only for the duration of the single statement using it

questions.title: Multiple CTEs Syntax
questions.description: How are two CTEs separated in one WITH clause?

questions.title: CTE Referenced Twice
questions.description: Can a CTE be referenced more than once inside its statement?
questions.Option2: Yes — the name may be referenced multiple times
questions.Option3: Only if UNION ALL is used

questions.title: Recursive Keyword
questions.description: Which keyword does SQLite require for a recursive CTE?

questions.title: Recursive CTE Shape
questions.description: A recursive CTE needs:
questions.Option1: An anchor SELECT plus a recursive SELECT combined with UNION ALL (or UNION)

questions.title: Recursion Stop Condition
questions.description: When does a recursive CTE stop producing rows?
questions.Option3: When the recursive SELECT produces no new rows
questions.Option4: When the base table is empty

questions.title: Sequence Generator Snippet
questions.description: What does this query return?
questions.codesnippet:
WITH RECURSIVE seq(n) AS (
  SELECT 1 UNION ALL
  SELECT n+1 FROM seq WHERE n < 5)
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM seq;

questions.title: UNION Versus UNION ALL In Recursion
questions.description: Inside a recursive CTE, using UNION instead of UNION ALL:
questions.Option4: Deduplicates intermediate rows, which can stop runaway chains

questions.title: Reading From The CTE
questions.description: After WITH x AS (SELECT ...), the main statement can:
questions.Option1: SELECT from x like a table
questions.Option4: Use x only in INSERT statements

questions.title: CTE Chaining Direction
questions.description: In WITH a AS (...), b AS (...), what may b reference?
questions.Option2: a (any earlier CTE) but not itself or later CTEs

questions.title: CTE Versus Subquery Readability
questions.description: The main benefit of a CTE over a subquery in FROM is:
questions.Option3: Named, reusable steps that make complex logic readable

questions.title: Two Single Row CTEs Snippet
questions.description: Is this statement valid SQLite?
questions.Option1: Yes — lo and hi are both defined and cross-joined in the main select
questions.Option3: No — MIN and MAX cannot appear in one WITH
questions.Option4: Only if UNION ALL is used

questions.title: Recursive Org Walk Snippet
questions.description: In this recursive CTE, what does the anchor SELECT pick?
questions.codesnippet:
WITH RECURSIVE chain(id, depth) AS (
  SELECT id, 1 FROM employees
    WHERE manager_id IS NULL
  UNION ALL
  SELECT e.id, c.depth+1
  FROM employees e JOIN chain c
    ON e.manager_id = c.id)
SELECT * FROM chain;

questions.title: Materialization Hint
questions.description: Since SQLite 3.35, how can you force a CTE to be materialized?

questions.title: CTE Column List Snippet
questions.description: In this statement, what are the CTE's column names?
questions.Option1: COUNT(*) and SUM(salary) — CTE columns keep the source expression names
questions.Option2: col1 and col2 — SQLite auto-generates default names
questions.Option3: The statement fails — a WITH clause cannot rename columns
questions.Option4: cnt and total — the WITH column list names the columns positionally

questions.title: Recursive Accumulator Snippet
questions.description: How many rows does this statement return?
questions.codesnippet:
WITH RECURSIVE t(n, total) AS (
  SELECT 1, 10 UNION ALL
  SELECT n+1, total+10 FROM t
  WHERE n < 3)
SELECT total FROM t ORDER BY n;

questions.title: Depth Guard Placement Snippet
questions.description: In this statement, why must the WHERE guard live inside the recursive member?
questions.Option1: Outer WHERE cannot see CTE columns
questions.Option2: It bounds how many rows the member produces — without it the sequence never ends
questions.Option3: SQLite requires WHERE in every SELECT
questions.codesnippet:
WITH RECURSIVE seq(n) AS (
  SELECT 1 UNION ALL
  SELECT n+1 FROM seq WHERE n < 4)
SELECT n FROM seq;

questions.title: CTE Join Back Snippet
questions.description: What does this statement return?
questions.Option3: Employees earning above their department's average
questions.codesnippet:
WITH dept_avg AS (
  SELECT department, AVG(salary) AS a
  FROM employees GROUP BY department)
SELECT e.name
FROM employees e JOIN dept_avg d
  ON d.department = e.department
WHERE e.salary > d.a;

questions.title: Runaway Recursion
questions.description: Removing WHERE n < 10 from a seq(n) = n + 1 recursive CTE causes:
questions.Option1: SQLite caps the result at 100 rows
questions.Option2: Runaway recursion — the member keeps producing rows forever
